says: next/: the jobs discovery law A5 over real SQLite passes `runs: 60` to `Arbitrary.checkEffect` as a number of its own, which decision 0535 refuses ("No law over real IO writes its own case count"), and `fabrika/runs-from-depth` does not see it, because the rule only counts a `runs` key inside an `arbitrary` object.
proof: `grep -n 'runs: 60' next/packages/libfabrika/src/jobs/JobsTest.ts` prints line 931, `{ seed: 119120, runs: 60, concurrency: 1 }`, and `pnpm lint` passes on it. The sibling law in `next/packages/libfabrika/src/ledger/LedgerStreamsTest.ts` line 98 writes the same call as `runs: runsFor({ fast: 30, full: 60 })`. `oxlint-plugins/runs-from-depth.ts` line 359 matches `runs` only when `inArbitrary(node)`.
cost: A law over real IO can keep a fixed count no depth setting reaches, and the lint rule meant to hold 0535 misses the `Arbitrary.checkEffect` form.
